title: Saffron quantile-tail investigation and burst mitigation
content:
Summary:

This note captures the Saffron POC investigation into quantile (p50/p95/p99) behavior during microburst traffic, how KV cache warming interacts with varied sequence lengths, and cost impact of different mitigation strategies. The POC goal is to recommend a deployable configuration profile for Saffron's hybrid inference workload (chat + short generation) that meets p95 SLA of 250ms while minimizing per-token cost.

Context and goals:
- Customer: Saffron (ecommerce personalization, global traffic, mid-market).
- Target SLA: p95 <= 250ms for single-shot chat/generation; 99th percentile guidance <= 800ms.
- Workload: 70% short (<=32 tokens) chat completions, 25% medium (33-128 tokens), 5% long (>128 tokens).
- Traffic profile: baseline qps 180, periodic microbursts up to 1200 qps for ~30s (peak every ~12min).
- Primary questions: Which combination of warmstart, prefix caching, batching settings, and quantization keeps p95 within SLA during bursts while minimizing cost? What fallback strategy is robust?

Testbed and configuration:
- Runtime: internal GPU serving runtime (experimental branch with improved KV prefetch, see PR #2148).
- Hardware: a mix of A100-40GB and H100-80GB nodes; tests here run on H100 pool (8 GPUs, 2 instances), with an emulated cold pool on A100 for fallback validation.
- Models: Saffron-7B-v2 (FP16 and int8 quantized variants).
- Key variables: batch window (ms), max batch size, prefix/KV cache TTL, warmstart ratio (percent warm containers), quantized vs fp16 model selection, route fallback policy.

Workload synthesis:
- Synthetic traffic generator used to recreate real user bursts: poisson baseline with scheduled spike windows using ramp-up 2s to peak, 30s hold, ramp-down 3s.
- Sequence length distribution sampled from Saffron telemetry (reduced noise): short: 0.7, medium: 0.25, long: 0.05.
- Two mix variants: "even-chat" (more short-turn chats) and "mixed-gen" (higher medium/long proportion) tested across runs.
- Cold vs warm start scenarios: cold = empty KV cache and 0% warm containers; warm = pre-warmed KV caches and 70% warm containers.

Key measurements collected:
- p50 / p95 / p99 latencies (end-to-end request time).
- Token/sec throughput and GPU utilization per instance.
- KV cache hit ratio and miss latency contribution.
- Cost estimate based on instance-hour consumption and effective token rate (model per-token cost multiplier for quantized vs fp16).

Selected results (representative runs):
1) Baseline (no warmstart, batch_window=20ms, max_batch=64, fp16):
   - baseline QPS 180: p50 42ms, p95 310ms, p99 620ms
   - burst 1200 QPS: p50 88ms, p95 1120ms, p99 > 2500ms (many timeouts)
   - KV hit ratio: 18% during first 60s of burst; GPU utilization spiked then fell due to queueing.
   - Notes: unacceptable p95 under burst.

2) Warmstart + prefix cache enabled (warm containers 70%, batch_window=10ms, max_batch=64, fp16):
   - baseline: p50 38ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms
   - burst: p50 72ms, p95 280ms, p99 780ms
   - KV hit ratio: 72% during burst; cold evictions limited by TTL tuning.
   - Cost: +22% instance-hours vs baseline but p95 within SLA for this scenario.

3) Aggressive batching (batch_window=40ms, max_batch=128) with warmstart:
   - baseline: p50 46ms, p95 240ms, p99 580ms
   - burst: p50 92ms, p95 430ms, p99 1200ms
   - Observed batching reduces per-token cost ~18% but increases p95 beyond SLA during bursts because queueing latency dominates for short requests.

4) Quantized int8 fallback for overloads (warmstart fp16 primary, int8 fallback route when queue depth > threshold):
   - baseline (fp16 prim): p95 215ms; under burst, when fallback enabled and triggered, p95 observed 295ms (combined); cost estimate decreased ~15% relative to pure fp16 warmstart case.
   - tradeoff: minor quality degradation observed for 2% of queries (detected by eval harness); acceptable per Saffron acceptance criteria if limited to high-queue windows.

5) KV-prefetch + microburst smoothing window (local token prefetch for active user sessions + smoothing at ingress to avoid 2s ramp spikes):
   - combined with warmstart: p95 under burst 260ms -> 230ms (smoothing reduced instantaneous peaks); cost +8% vs warmstart baseline.

Analysis and insights:
- Warm containers and a healthy prefix/KV cache are the single biggest lever to bring p95 into SLA during short microbursts. In our runs, moving from 0% to ~70% warm containers shifted p95 during bursts from 1120ms -> 280ms.
- Aggressive batching reduces unit cost but harms short-tail latency. For Saffron's heavy short-request mix, batching windows >20ms are detrimental. Recommendation: keep batch_window <= 15ms for primary route.
- Quantized model fallback is effective as a capacity knob: when used only for high-queue situations it preserves p95 and trims cost. Need guardrails: evaluation harness and automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed 1.5% of invocations.
- KV cache eviction and TTL are critical. Default TTL (30s) led to high miss rates under repeated bursts. Extending TTL to 5min increased hit ratio significantly but increases memory usage; recommend dynamic TTL per customer session frequency.

Recommendations for Saffron POC deployment profile (initial):
- Primary route: fp16 Saffron-7B-v2 with warmstart 65-75% containers, batch_window=10ms, max_batch=64, KV prefix cache TTL=300s, autoscale target qps per GPU tuned conservatively (+10% over observed peak).
- Overload policy: queue-depth based fallback to int8 variant with graceful degradation window (max 30% of traffic routed to int8 during sustained overload).
- Ingress smoothing: implement burst-smoothing token-bucket at LB to spread ramp over 2-3s for scheduled peaks if possible (client changes may be needed).
- Observability: p50/p95/p99 per-route and per-model, KV hit ratio, queue depth heatmaps, and quality sample checks (periodic inline eval of sampled outputs comparing fp16 vs int8).
- Cost projection: expected +18-25% instance-hours vs cold baseline, but overall per-token cost ~5-10% lower than pure cold with missed SLA penalties avoided.

Open questions and risks:
- Long-form generations (>128 tokens) inflate GPU utilization and lower effective throughput; need a separate dedicated pool or stricter routing to avoid affecting short-chat latency.
- Memory pressure from extended KV TTL on H100 fleet—observe in staging with scaled session counts. Possible mitigation: hybrid TTL where TTL scales with session activity score.
- Quality guard for int8 fallback: need automated rollback and A/B quality checks in console to ensure customer acceptance.

Next steps / action items:
- (Ravi) Run a 72-hour soak with TTL=300s and warmstart 70% on a 16-GPU staging cluster and collect extended telemetry (due 2029-03-28, linear SE-7329).
- (Liam) Implement queue-depth trigger policy as described and a sampling hook for inline quality checks (PR referenced: runtime#2148).
- (Noor) Draft Saffron-facing brief with recommended profile and expected cost delta; include simple runbook for rollback during initial 2-week deployment window.
- (Evan) Validate KV memory footprint on H100 fleet with 3M active sessions synthetic run.

Appendix: sample raw numbers from representative 1200qps burst run (warmstart 70%, batch_window=10ms, max_batch=64):
- total requests: 36,800 (30s window repeated 3 times)
- p50: 72ms, p95: 280ms, p99: 780ms
- average tokens/request: 34
- GPU utilization avg: 78%, peak 96%
- KV hit ratio: 72% overall during burst, miss latency contribution avg 120ms for misses
- Estimated cost: wage of instances equivalent -> projected incremental $0.012 per 1k tokens (quantized fallback offload reduces to $0.010 per 1k tokens on similar runs)

Notes to reviewers: this is an interactive lab-note doc — rely on raw telemetry attached in linked_artifacts for numeric validation. The recommendations favor a conservative warmstart-first approach with quantized fallback as a secondary lever. If Saffron prioritizes cost over strict p95 SLA, a different profile (bigger batching window + larger int8 pool) can be suggested — call that out explicitly in the customer brief.

End of note.
